title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment in Australia. After kidney stone surgery in March, she read a post-operative letter to her GP that falsely stated she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms, which she has never done. She was upset and worried because she was receiving workers' compensation and feared the error could affect her case. She complained, and the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A privacy watchdog report found AI medical scribes can hallucinate false symptoms, with examples including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and inventing epilepsy. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use these tools. Australia's medical regulator says doctors must check all AI output. The Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing AI scribes and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Advocacy groups want approved tool lists and stronger safeguards.
